name: Advanced Sanitize
description: Config-file-driven database anonymizer: replaces entity-field and raw-table values in place with FakerPHP fakes, constants, or SQL expressions, run from a settings form or a Drush command.
project_description: Advanced Sanitize is a developer tool that anonymizes data already in a Drupal database, typically after copying a production database into a development or staging environment. Instead of hooking into Drush's core sql:sanitize, it reads a developer-authored YAML definition file (path set at /admin/config/development/sanitize-settings) and rewrites the listed values in place. Two record shapes are supported: Drupal entity records (entity_id + bundle_id + field_mapping, processed through the Entity API with entity save) and raw SQL-table records (table_name + unique_column + column_mapping, processed with direct UPDATE queries). Each mapped field or column names a data provider: 'faker' (any FakerPHP method, with optional locale and parameters), 'constant' (a fixed replacement value) or 'expression' (a raw SQL expression, table records only). Options let you skip specific entity ids or field values (ignore_entity_id / ignore_field_values) and force uniqueness (ensure_unique prepends a uniqid). Work runs through the Batch API with configurable per-batch limits, and seven events (started, preprocess-definition, pre/post entity sanitize, pre/post revision sanitize, finished) let other code observe or alter the run. Launch it from the settings form's Sanitize button or the Drush command advanced_sanitize:sanitize (alias adsan). It depends only on the fakerphp/faker library and provides its own admin permission, config schema, and Drush command.
